{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Contractor Services Agreement (Clear Capital / RadialSpark) 
**Status:** All findings below are verified; two were repaired during verification (NOSOLICIT, LOL-CAP).

---

## 1. Executive summary

The commercial architecture of this agreement works in our favour and we should say so plainly at the table: engagement is task-by-task under Statements of Work, compensation is pure time-and-materials, and there is **no** exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment, MFN, liquidated-damages, auto-renewal or Vendor audit right anywhere in the document. Ownership is also strong — § 4(a) vests all invoiced-and-paid Works (including data, programs and documentation) in the Company, § 4(b) leaves the Contractor only its own pre-existing tools, and §§ 5(b)/8 keep our data and Confidential Information out of Contractor's hands. We are not proposing changes to any of that.

The gaps are concentrated in risk allocation and exit. Two items are critical or near-critical: **§ 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but contains no indemnity language at all** — a full-document search for "indemn" returns only that heading — leaving us with no IP defence beyond the bare non-infringement warranty in § 5(c); and the § 7(a) cap contains no usable carve-out, because its sole exception points to "Paragraph 9", which in this document is the Independent Contractor clause. Alongside these, we have no right to exit an active Statement of Work for convenience, no transition assistance or data-return obligation on termination, no conformance warranty or repair/replace/refund remedy, no successor-assignment carve-out, no cyber insurance, and an Arizona governing law paired with mandatory arbitration and no venue clause.

Ten of nineteen findings are compliant and require no redline. Nine require action, and our proposals are drafted at the fallback level wherever the fallback is achievable, so the negotiation surface is deliberately narrow.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Short point |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Heading only; no indemnity language exists. Walk-away territory. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | At or above fallback; we own paid-for Works, perpetual sublicensable licence to Contractor's embedded Information. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | No sole-supplier or requirements obligation; task-by-task SOWs. Preferred position met. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 Termination | No LDs, minimum fees or early-termination charge; only fees actually earned. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | § 4(c) is perpetual and sublicensable but no affiliate coverage and no successor transfer (§ 10 consent). |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | No non-compete, territory or field-of-use covenant binds Company. |
| 7 | Medium | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | § 10 is mutual and reasonable but captures M&A successors; no change-of-control trigger to delete. |
| 8 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No Vendor audit, inspection or verification right at all — better than fallback. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Arizona law (outside accepted list); § 19 mandatory arbitration; no venue clause. |
| 10 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No best-price, benchmarking or price-matching obligation on Company. |
| 11 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No minimum, volume or take-or-pay commitment; pay only for services ordered. |
| 12 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** *(repaired)* | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | § 13 is mutual and involvement-limited, but runs term plus one year and has no advertising/unsolicited carve-outs. |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | Evergreen term with mutual 15-day convenience exit when no SOW outstanding; no auto-renewal. |
| 14 | Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 6 Termination | § 6(a) convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding; no Customer exit from active work, no refund. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 6 Termination | No transition assistance, data return/export or deletion obligation anywhere. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer | Only legality, authority and non-infringement; no conformance warranty, period or remedy, with implieds disclaimed. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | § 14 meets fallback E&O at USD 1,000,000 but has no cyber/privacy coverage. |
| 18 | Low | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** *(repaired)* | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual, but based on total fees paid rather than 12 months, and the only exception points to the Independent Contractor clause. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

**Absence of any Contractor IP indemnity (§ 7, INDEMN — critical).** This is the one finding recorded as sitting in walk-away territory. The section is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" yet contains only liability caps (7(a)), a damages exclusion (7(b)) and a fee waiver (7(c)); the sole IP hook is the § 5(c) non-infringement warranty, which carries no defence obligation, no indemnity and no remedies. We are inserting a fallback-level Contractor IP indemnity with the usual Company modification/combination/specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace and refund remedies, and a 3x annual fees super-cap, and conforming the § 7(a) cap so it does not swallow that super-cap. We are deliberately **not** adding a Company-side indemnity, since none exists today and adding one would only weaken our position.

Two related items should be treated as travelling with the above, because the indemnity is worth little without them:

- **§ 7(a) has no usable carve-out.** Its only exception cross-refers to "Paragraph 9 hereof", which in this document is the Independent Contractor clause, so indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct all currently sit inside the cap.
- **No conformance warranty or remedy (§ 5).** With implied warranties disclaimed in lieu of three narrow express warranties, we have no contractual route to require correction of non-conforming deliverables.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Priority one — send with the first markup:**

1. **§ 7 — insert Contractor IP indemnity** with standard exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap; conform the liability cap exception (INDEMN).
2. **§ 7(a)/(b) — re-base both caps** to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and add a mutual, expressly uncapped Excluded Claims definition, preserving the existing Paragraph 9 exception verbatim (it benefits us). We leave untouched the asymmetry by which Contractor's cap is scoped to Services under a SOW while ours covers the Agreement generally — that favours us (LOL-CAP).
3. **§ 5 — add the fallback conformance warranty**: 90 days for software/deliverables, 30 days for Services, with repair, replacement or refund. We are not pursuing the preferred 12-month/no-malicious-code package (WARRANTY).

**Priority two — exit and continuity:**

4. **§ 6 — add a Company-only convenience termination right** on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. Contractor's side already conforms, since it cannot exercise convenience while a SOW is outstanding; we note but do not redline that its 15-day notice in the no-SOW shell period is shorter than our preferred 90 days (T4C).
5. **§ 6 — insert a wind-down paragraph**: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Company Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter (TRANSITION).

**Priority three — clean-up, low expected resistance:**

6. **§ 4(c) — append affiliate coverage on written notice and successor transferability** to the licence grant, leaving the grant language and § 10 otherwise intact (LICENSE).
7. **§ 10 — add a mutual successor-assignment carve-out** on written notice for merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, preserving the existing consent and reasonableness mechanics (ASSIGN).
8. **Governing law / § 19 — move to New York law** and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with the customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out, and conform the § 19 heading so no arbitration mechanic is left dangling (GOVLAW).
9. **§ 14 — add cyber/privacy liability coverage of USD 2,000,000**, the single shortest fallback-level addition. Contractor holds our Confidential Information and may access our systems under § 1(c). Preferred-only shortfalls (no CGL aggregate figure, E&O at USD 1,000,000, no post-term tail) are noted but not redlined (INSURANCE).

**Points to track without redlining:** Contractor's unilateral right to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap (§ 3(b)) is a mid-term pricing mechanic and falls outside the RENEWAL and MINCOMMIT rules; flag it commercially if the engagement is expected to run long. Also worth noting for the negotiation record is the dangling § 7(a) cross-reference to Paragraph 9 and the stray § 6(c) at p0044, both of which suggest the draft has been assembled from an earlier template — we should ask the Contractor to confirm no indemnity or transition text was intended to be included and dropped.

**Ask of the business:** confirm the expected engagement length and whether prepayment is contemplated, as both drive the value of items 2 and 4."}
